name: Marcus Faraone
temperament: argues — turns it into a debate
neighborhood: Chinatown; his 'place' is the abandoned grain silos on the Pier 80 side of the port
tags: knows the port's abandoned buildings by memory

focus.name: 9mm SIG P365, concealed-carry
focus.description: Bought two months before Ep 1 after being jumped and mugged near his warehouse; he got the CCP through the warehouse's security-role paperwork afterwards, and it's still fresh enough that he re-reads the permit conditions when he's nervous. **The permit issued about six months before Ep 5** — recent enough that anyone who runs his ID can see it is new. In-domain: standing in a room in a way that changes the room, walking through a door as if he owns it.
focus.inFlightVariant: Mars could not carry the pistol on an international flight to Taiwan (Taiwanese law is severe). In Ep 1 he carried the holster clip on his keychain — a muscle-memory anchor for the weapon he wasn't wearing. Same domain, same focus by cognitive-anchor logic; the object he touches when he needs to feel his own shape in a room. Since returning home (Ep 2 onward), he carries the pistol again.
focus.rangeHabit: He went to the range four or five times in the first weeks, seriously, with the focus of someone doing homework. He has been maybe twice since. **The pistol is an anchor, not a skill** — the object he touches to feel his own shape in a room — and he is quietly aware that he is not especially good with it. He does not volunteer this. If a scene asks whether he trains, this is the answer unless his player says otherwise; do NOT drift him toward competence, because his Phase-2 release moment is standing his ground WITHOUT it.

meaningfulItem: 9mm SIG P365, concealed-carry — bought two months before Ep 1 after being jumped near the warehouse. In-flight variant: the holster clip on his keychain when he can't carry.
specificPlace: The abandoned grain silos on the Pier 80 side of the port — he knows every catwalk by memory.
intentionUnderPressure: My mother lived in that Dogpatch apartment thirty years. She was priced out last year. The paperwork was clean, the notice was legal, and I couldn't stop it. Afterward I started organizing on the side, because the next old woman on the block isn't going to lose her place because nobody was standing there when the notice came.
backstory:
Mars grew up in Dogpatch and has watched every wave of development eat the neighborhood he learned to walk in. He enrolled at SF State's business school at 18, dropped out at 20 when the money got tight, took a warehouse job that was supposed to be temporary, and has been there five years. He runs the shift now. He started organizing on the side after his mother was priced out of her apartment of thirty years last year.

Two months before Ep 1, he was jumped outside the Pier 80 gate at 4am end-of-shift. Two men, one hit, one grabbed the wallet. He was on the ground for a minute before he could stand up. He was fine. He wasn't fine. He bought the pistol the following week and got the permit through work.

He met Morgan on a War Thunder forum eight months ago; they became close friends over long late-night voice calls where Morgan doesn't talk about 'the industry' and Mars doesn't talk about the mugging. The Taipei trip was Morgan's idea and Mars's excuse — he was burnt out, wanted to disappear for a couple weeks, and Morgan was going anyway.

Height has been the single most consistent fact of his social life since sixth grade. He does not talk about it. If you bring it up, he will out-argue you and remember.

bonds.name: Morgan Reyes
bonds.description: The War Thunder friend, Taipei co-conspirator. Closer than either says.

bonds: **Alaia Vega** — the Bodie ranger. She remembered him making cocoa at the Union Hall, and when Dakota's antics stalled at Caffè Strada she spent a long stretch talking with Mars instead. Two people who are responsible for others at work.

dmNotes.intentionUnderPressureNote: The Dogpatch eviction that pushed him into tenant organizing is the fictional root of his presence-domain casting: 'standing in a room in a way that changes the room' is literally *nobody was standing there when the notice came*. The mugging is the cost-signature (neck-flare) — different beat, different function. Phase-2 release moment candidate: a scene where he stands his ground without the pistol on him, and the room re-shapes anyway — proof to himself that the presence is his, not the weapon's.
dmNotes.castDomain: posture / presence — a bouncer stands down, an angry crowd finds a smaller target, a threat re-thinks. Presence-domain casts look 'just like being charismatic' from outside; the fictional cost is Mars sleeping badly and a next-day flare of the neck injury from the mugging. Player triggers cast by describing both stance AND intent (the WHY, not just the WHAT).
dmNotes.costTellPolicy: The neck-flare (mugging-at-Pier-80 cost signature) fires prominently on FIRST cast and on Costly-tier or higher casts. For Cheap/Free-tier casts, log privately; mention on-page at DM's discretion, roughly 1 in 3. Overuse tedious; underuse loses the pattern.
dmNotes.bringAGunWatch: Mars may want to bring the pistol into scenes where it doesn't help. Give him graceful ways to *not*. Some venues (state parks, government offices) will notice a concealed carry — a real logistical friction, not a moral one.
dmNotes.alignmentDriftWatch: Could drift toward Chaotic Good the more he protects the party. Could drift toward Neutral Evil if the mugging trauma routes into a revenge fixation.
dmNotes.focusNotes: If the pistol is confiscated in-scene, Mars needs to find a stand-in fast — the holster clip on his keychain is still the fallback, per Ep 1 mechanic.

markLog.criterion: Acted against your own short-term interest because the story demanded it
markLog.note: A man who sits with his back to a wall, on a long flight, among strangers — and stayed in it rather than withdrawing.

markLog.criterion: Learned something true about The Quiet, the world, or another character
markLog.note: The In-N-Out. He reads people for a living and he watched Reggie be frightened of a name, which told the party more than the footage did.

markLog.criterion: Took a meaningful risk for someone else
markLog.note: Blizzard logistics. The warehouse supervisor is the one who works out what a trapped group physically needs and then goes and does it.

markLog.criterion: Resolved a hard moment by acting in line with alignment
markLog.note: The door at Vivian's. His first attempt fumbled when Priya interrupted; he regrouped, leaned on the railing and named the honest thing — that he needed to see for himself. Elena let all five in. He does not know he cast anything.

markLog.criterion: Took on a complication or scar that will matter later
markLog.note: A concealed-carry permit holder logged at Park Station that morning and standing inside an unlawfully entered house that evening.
